recipe.name: Kerala Chicken Curry with Green Mango

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Cut the chicken breast into pieces. Slice the onion, mince the ginger and garlic, and slit the serrano chile.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and soften the onion with the ginger, garlic and chile.
Stir in the cumin, coriander powder, turmeric and cayenne and fry for a minute until the raw smell goes.
Add the chicken and brown it, then pour in the coconut milk and simmer 12 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Cut the mango into firm chunks and add it for the last 5 minutes only, so it holds its shape and stays tart rather than dissolving into sweetness.
Scatter with the chopped cilantro and serve over the rice.

note: 'Mango Chicken Curry' has no traditional form, so per the report it was converted into a dish that does: a Kerala-style curry using raw/green mango as the souring agent rather than ripe mango as a sweetener. Added the missing ginger, garlic, chile and cilantro, and a real cooking fat - step 3 previously said 'saute onion in oil' with no fat in the ingredient list at all. Garam masala dropped (a North Indian finishing blend that does not belong in a coconut-based Kerala curry) and the mango moved to the last 5 minutes. Brown Rice to White Rice, which is what Kerala curries are eaten with.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.

Rinse the toor dal and boil it with the turmeric, a little salt and about 1 1/4 cups of water until soft, roughly 20 minutes, then whisk it smooth. Cooking the turmeric with the lentils is what colours the dal itself rather than just the topping.
Dice the onion, chop the tomato, mince the garlic and ginger and slit the serrano chile.
Heat the butter in a small pan until it foams, then crackle the cumin in it - this is the tadka, and it starts with whole spice in hot fat, not with onion.
Add the garlic, ginger and chile and fry to pale gold, then the onion until golden, then the tomato and chili powder and cook it down 2 minutes.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the cooked dal, stir it through, season with black pepper, and finish with the chopped cilantro. Serve with the rice.

note: The dish is named after the tadka and the tadka was not one - it started with onion in butter instead of whole spice crackled in hot fat, so that order is now correct. Red Lentils to Toor Dal, which is the classic dal for tadka and which Phase A added. Turmeric moved into the boiling lentils where it belongs. Jarred Tomato Sauce to fresh Tomato, plus the missing ginger, chile and cilantro. Cooking liquid rescaled from 2.5 cups to about 1 1/4 cups - 40 g of dry lentils in 2.5 cups is roughly 15:1 and makes soup. Brown Rice to White Rice, since dal-chawal is white rice.

steps: Slice the onion thin and fry it in the vegetable oil until deep golden and crisp. Lift it out onto paper - this is the birista, and it is folded through the dish rather than used as decoration.

Cube the lamb shoulder. Marinate it in the greek yogurt with the minced garlic and ginger, the cumin, garam masala, black pepper, salt, the lemon juice, half the birista, half the mint and half the cilantro.
Wash and soak the basmati rice 10 minutes, then parboil it with the cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf until 70% cooked. Drain.
Cook the marinated lamb in a heavy pot until the yogurt tightens around the meat and the fat separates, about 20 minutes.
Steep the saffron in a spoonful of warm water.
Layer the parboiled rice over the lamb. Scatter the remaining birista, mint and cilantro over the top and drizzle the saffron water across the surface.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat 15-20 minutes, then fluff gently from the edge inward and serve.

note: Ground lamb was the disqualifying problem - biryani is chunks of bone-in lamb layered with rice, and mince makes it a keema pulao. Kept the name and changed the meat to Lamb Shoulder, which Phase A added (the report thought it was unavailable). Added the two things that actually define the dish and were both missing: birista (deep-fried onions folded through) and saffron steeped and drizzled over the top layer. Added ginger, mint, cilantro and lemon. Turmeric dropped - biryani takes its colour from saffron and fried onion, and turmeric muddies it toward yellow.

steps: Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Blanch the spinach and mustard greens for a minute, then drop them into ice water to hold the colour.
Blend the greens with the ginger, garlic and serrano chile into a coarse puree - the aromatics go into the puree, not into the pan afterwards.
Dice the onion, chop the tomato and cut the chicken breast into pieces.
Crackle the cumin in the vegetable oil, then fry the onion until golden and add the tomato and cook it down.
Add the chicken and brown it, then stir in the greens puree with the turmeric, coriander powder and garam masala and simmer 15 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the greek yogurt so it enriches the sauce without splitting, then scatter the cilantro over.
Serve over the rice.

note: Two ingredients did not belong in a chicken dish and both are gone: Paneer (chicken and paneer in one bowl is not a North Indian pairing) and Cauliflower. Added Mustard Greens, which Phase A added and which is what makes the name 'Saag' honest - saag means mixed winter greens, not spinach alone, and the dish as written was palak. Added the garlic and ginger it had none of, plus tomato and cilantro, and a real cooking fat, since step 4 said 'saute onion' with no fat listed. The yogurt now goes in off the heat instead of being simmered 15 minutes, which would split it. Protein drops about 8 g with the paneer gone, as the report predicted; still 65 g and comfortably high-protein.

steps: Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Slice the onion thin and fry it in the butter until deep golden, then lift most of it out and grind it to a paste - this fried-onion paste is the structural backbone of a korma and the dish had none.
Cut the chicken breast into pieces. Mince the garlic and ginger and slit the serrano chile.
Fry the garlic, ginger and chile in the remaining butter, add the chicken and seal it, then stir in the cumin, coriander powder, cardamom and cinnamon.

Whisk the gram flour into the greek yogurt, then stir it into the pan off the heat and return it to a bare simmer - the besan stabilises the yogurt so it thickens the sauce instead of splitting, and it does the job almond or cashew paste would do in a traditional korma.
Stir the fried-onion paste back in and simmer gently 12 minutes until the sauce coats the chicken. Season with salt, black pepper and white pepper.
Scatter with the chopped cilantro and serve over the rice.

note: Took the report's recommended Mughlai lane. Coconut milk removed - it belongs to a South Indian kurma, and having it alongside cardamom and cinnamon fused two cuisines in one bowl. Added the fried-onion paste that is the korma's backbone, plus garlic and ginger, and a real fat (step 3 said 'saute onion in oil' with nothing in the list). Turmeric dropped: a korma is deliberately pale. A traditional korma is thickened with almond or cashew paste, which is banned here, so Gram Flour (Besan) does that job instead - it also keeps the yogurt from splitting. Besan is a Phase A row the report thought unavailable.

steps: Toast the gram flour in a dry pan for a minute, then whisk it into the greek yogurt with the minced ginger and garlic, the cumin, turmeric, garam masala, coriander powder, paprika, salt and black pepper. The besan is what makes the marinade cling to the paneer instead of sliding off.
Cut the paneer into cubes and fold it through the marinade. Leave it 15 minutes.
Cut the bell pepper and onion into squares.
Grill or pan-sear the paneer and vegetables until charred at the edges.
Squeeze the lemon over the hot paneer and toss through the chopped cilantro.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan, pile the paneer and vegetables down the middle, roll it up tightly and serve.

note: This is a kathi roll and the marinade was missing its besan, which is what makes a paneer tikka marinade cling rather than slide off - Phase A added Gram Flour (Besan). Added ginger, garlic, cilantro and a lemon finish (the squeeze over hot paneer is the signature). Chili Powder replaced with Paprika, which is the closest legal stand-in for the Kashmiri chili that gives paneer tikka its red without heat. The tortilla stays: a paratha wrapper would be more correct but there is no paratha row, and Greek Yogurt is already a good hung-curd stand-in.

steps: Cut deep diagonal slashes into the chicken thigh, down to the bone. Rub it with half the lemon juice, the salt and a little of the paprika and leave it 15 minutes - this first marinade is what seasons the meat itself.
Whisk the greek yogurt with the minced garlic and ginger, the cumin, garam masala, the rest of the paprika, the cayenne, black pepper and the olive oil.
Coat the slashed chicken in the yogurt marinade, working it into the cuts, and refrigerate as long as you can - four hours if possible, overnight is better.
Grill or bake at 220C for 15-20 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the basmati rice and slice the onion into rings.
Squeeze the remaining lemon over the chicken and serve with the rice and the raw onion rings.

note: Rebuilt on the canonical two-marinade method: a first rub of lemon, salt and chili directly into deep slashes cut to the bone, then the yogurt marinade over it. Without the slashes the marinade only ever coats the outside. Added ginger (garlic was there, ginger is the missing half of the pair) and a fat in the marinade. Turmeric dropped - it dulls the red toward orange-brown and is not a tandoori spice. Paprika deliberately KEPT rather than swapped: the report wants Kashmiri chili powder, which is not in the vocabulary, and paprika is precisely the mild red-colour stand-in for it. Marinating time corrected from 10 minutes, which every source rejects.

blocked.wanted: whole-spice and finishing vocabulary the reports lean on heavily: Mustard Seeds, Curry Leaves, Fenugreek, Asafoetida, Cloves, Black Cardamom, Kasuri Methi, Ajwain, Chaat Masala, Fennel Seeds, Kashmiri Chili Powder
blocked.did: none are in the frozen vocabulary. Used Paprika for Kashmiri chili (its exact purpose - red colour without heat), Cayenne where real heat was wanted, and Serrano Chile for green chili. The rest are omitted; they are aromatics rather than structural, and every structural fix landed.

blocked.wanted: almond or cashew paste, the traditional Mughlai thickener
blocked.did: banned by the no-nuts constraint. Used Gram Flour (Besan), which thickens and also stabilises the yogurt against splitting - the report named besan as the nut-free route.

blocked.recipe: Lamb Biryani / Saag Chicken / Dal Tadka / Paneer Tikka Wrap
blocked.wanted: Lamb Shoulder, Mustard Greens, Toor Dal, Gram Flour (Besan), all flagged by the report as NOT in registry
blocked.did: all four ARE in the registry - Phase A added them. The report's notes were written pre-Phase-A and are stale. Used all four.

_summary.notes: Written inline by the main session after the slice-08 agent was killed by a session limit at 6 of 13. Its first six records are intact in 08-indian.jsonl; these are the remaining seven. One rename: Mango Chicken Curry -> Kerala Chicken Curry with Green Mango (one of the five approved rebuilds). No cuisine relabels - British-Indian was not needed, since the two candidates (tikka masala, korma) were handled by the first agent and by the Mughlai rebuild respectively.
